subject: storytime
title: The Tale of Tom Kitten
about: Beatrix Potter's 1907 tale of Tom Kitten and his sisters Mittens and Moppet, dressed in their best clothes for their mother's tea party and told to stay clean, who lose every button and stitch on the garden wall to three waddling Puddle-Ducks. First graders love the pop of the buttons, the pit-pat waddle-pat refrain and the thumping upstairs while the grown-ups sip their tea. It is a public-domain book retold here in first-grade words, five pages long; the real one with Potter's pictures is at the library.
tip: Chant pit-pat, paddle-pat with him, then ask who ended up wearing the kittens' clothes.

book.author: Beatrix Potter (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: Three kittens, their best clothes, and three cheeky ducks.

passage.text:
Once there were three little kittens.
Their names were Mittens, Tom Kitten, and Moppet.
Their mother was Mrs. Tabitha Twitchit.
One day, friends were coming for tea.
So she washed their faces.
She brushed their fur.
She put them in their best clothes.
Tom's suit had six shiny buttons.
"Now go out and play," she said.
"But keep your clothes clean!"
***
The kittens went out into the garden.
Moppet and Mittens tried to stay clean.
But they tripped on their long dresses.
Tom could not even hop.
His suit was too tight!
Then they climbed up the garden wall.
Pop! Pop! Pop!
Tom's buttons flew off one by one.
***
Just then, three ducks came waddling by.
Pit-pat, paddle-pat! Pit-pat, waddle-pat!
They were the Puddle-Ducks.
"Look at all the buttons!" said a duck.
Then Tom's hat fell off the wall.
His suit slid off, too.
The dresses slipped off next.
Soon all the clothes were in a heap.
The ducks picked them up.
And they put them on!
***
Off went the ducks in the fine clothes.
Pit-pat, paddle-pat! Pit-pat, waddle-pat!
Splash!
They jumped into the pond.
The clothes floated away.
The three kittens sat on the wall.
They had no clothes on at all!
Just then, Mrs. Tabitha Twitchit came out.
"Oh my!" she said.
"Look at you!"
"My friends are coming for tea!"
She was very upset.
***
She sent the kittens upstairs.
"Stay up there and be good," she said.
Then her friends came for tea.
They sat and sipped and talked.
But the kittens were not being good.
Thump! Bump! Thump!
They bounced on the beds.
What a noisy tea party!
And the Puddle-Ducks?
They are still looking for those clothes.

cards.note: Tabitha Twitchit is the mother of Tom, Mittens and Moppet; the three ducks are the Puddle-Ducks.

cards.q: What did the mother tell the kittens to do?
cards.note: That is the one thing she asks, and it lasts about as long as a walk to the garden wall.
Pop, pop, pop: the suit was too tight, so the buttons flew off one by one.

cards.q: Who put on the kittens' clothes?
cards.note: The ducks picked up the heap of clothes, put them on and waddled off to the pond.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: Washed faces, brushed fur and best clothes come first; the garden wall undoes it all.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: The friends sipped tea downstairs while thump, bump, thump went the kittens upstairs.

cards.q: How did the kittens' mother feel when she saw them?
cards.note: Oh my, look at you: her friends were on the way and the kittens had nothing on.

cards.q: Where did the kittens go out to play?
cards.note: The setting is where a story happens: a house with a garden, a wall and a pond.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'waddling' mean?
cards.note: Ducks rock from side to side when they walk: pit-pat, waddle-pat.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
